A personal transformation system · food + training · vegetarian · one electric skillet · one hostel gym
Eat well in a hostel.Get lighter, stronger, and harder to tire.
A sustainable, high-protein, high-fibre meal system paired with a 24-week progressive training plan — built for a 20-year-old vegetarian student in a hostel whose entire kitchen is a multipurpose electric skillet (it sautés, boils, steams and crisps) and whose gym is the hostel gym. The food supports insulin sensitivity, hormonal balance and steady fat loss; the training preserves muscle and builds stamina, strength, mobility, posture and a core that actually holds you up. This is a system for months, not a diet for weeks.

~1,450–1,650 kcal/day
70–90 g protein
30 g+ fibre

Train 6 days/week
No crash dieting

Page 01 · Introduction
How this plan works
This is a system, not a diet. Every day follows the same rhythm — wake-up drink, a solid cooked breakfast at 9, a packed box at 1:30, the real cooked lunch at 6 pm when you’re back at the skillet, a small dessert, a light 9:30 dinner, and a calming night drink. Around it runs a 6-day training week at the hostel gym. The food and workouts change; the structure never does. That predictability is what makes it survivable in a hostel for six months.

🎯 The goalRoughly 20 kg over ~6 months means averaging about 0.7–0.8 kg per week. Early weeks often move faster (water weight), later weeks slower. A realistic healthy range is 0.5–1 kg/week — this plan aims for the middle, with muscle preserved and built through high protein plus the progressive strength work in the training plan. The scale is only one of ten things you'll track.
🔥 The deficitMost young Indian women maintain weight around 1,900–2,200 kcal/day when moderately active. This plan lands at ~1,450–1,650 kcal — a moderate, sustainable deficit. No starving, no skipped meals, no "detoxes". Hunger is managed with protein, fibre, volume and one daily dessert.
🍳 The constraintEvery recipe works with a multipurpose electric skillet — its flat hot surface sautés vegetables, paneer and tofu with barely any oil, boils dal, rice, pasta and noodles, steams in a small basket, and dry-crisps bread and chapatis — plus a small grinder, bowl, plate, knife, spoon and mug. Everything is cooked fresh and eaten the same day. The mess contributes exactly one thing: chapatis, smuggled and crisped.

How to use it: Follow Days 1–14, then repeat the cycle. Swap any breakfast for any breakfast, any 6pm lunch for any 6pm lunch, any light dinner for any light dinner — meals within a slot are calorie-matched, so swapping never breaks the plan. Shop small and often (no fridge = fresh daily dairy), restock the pantry monthly.

Page 02 · Important health notes
Read this before Day 1

About possible PCOS/PCOD
PCOS can only be diagnosed by a doctor (usually via symptoms + ultrasound + blood work such as fasting insulin, testosterone, LH/FSH and thyroid). If you have irregular periods, stubborn weight gain around the middle, acne, or excess hair growth, see a gynaecologist — a diagnosis changes nothing about this plan but may add medical options.
Whether or not it's PCOS, this plan is built around what reliably helps insulin resistance: protein at every meal, high fibre, low added sugar, whole-food carbs paired with protein/fat, regular meal timing, walking after meals, strength training, and sleep.

About your liver
Years of frequent junk food can contribute to non-alcoholic fatty liver, which is common, silent, and — importantly — usually reversible with gradual fat loss (even 5–10% of body weight helps significantly). Crash dieting can actually worsen it, which is another reason this plan is moderate.
Worth doing once: ask a doctor for a basic LFT (liver function test) and lipid profile. This plan already follows fatty-liver-friendly rules: minimal added sugar, no deep-fried food, no sugary drinks, more fibre, more whole foods.

Red lines

Never eat below ~1,400 kcal consistently — it backfires (muscle loss, hair fall, period disruption, rebound bingeing).
If your period becomes irregular or stops after starting the plan, eat slightly more and see a doctor.
Weight loss is not linear. Judge trends over 2–4 weeks, never day to day — water, salt, sleep and your cycle swing the scale by 1–2 kg.
During your period: keep the plan, be gentler with workouts, add iron-rich foods (spinach, dates, chana) + vitamin C (lemon) for absorption.

What this plan is not

Not medical advice — it's evidence-based general nutrition. Confirm anything specific with a registered dietitian or doctor.
No detoxes, cleanses, "fat-burner" teas, or miracle foods. They don't exist.
No food guilt. One heavy mess meal or a birthday cake slice changes nothing. The next meal is just the next meal.
Not a punishment. If a meal here doesn't taste good to you, swap it — sustainability beats perfection.

Page 03 · The science behind the plan
Why this works

Protein — the non-negotiableProtein preserves muscle in a deficit (muscle is your metabolism), has the highest thermic effect (your body burns ~20–30% of protein calories just digesting it), and is the most satiating macronutrient. Target: ~1.2–1.6 g per kg of goal body weight — here, roughly 70–90 g/day, split across every meal because your body uses it best in 20–30 g doses. Vegetarian sources leaned on: paneer, tofu, curd, dals, sprouts, soy chunks, sattu, peanuts, seeds, milk.
Fibre — the appetite off-switchFibre slows digestion, blunts blood-sugar spikes (critical if insulin resistance is present), feeds gut bacteria that regulate inflammation and even mood, and physically fills you. Target: 30 g+/day from vegetables, fruit with skin, oats, dals, chia, flax and whole grains. Increase gradually and drink water, or you'll bloat.
How PCOS changes the gameIn PCOS, many cells respond poorly to insulin, so the body releases more of it. High insulin makes fat storage easier, fat burning harder, and cravings stronger. The fixes are unglamorous but proven: never eat naked carbs (always pair with protein/fat/fibre), front-load protein at breakfast, walk 10 minutes after meals (muscles soak up glucose without insulin), lift weights, sleep 7–9 hours, manage stress. Fat loss with PCOS is slower, not impossible — expect the same result on a longer timeline.
Sleep — the hidden macroShort sleep (<7 h) raises ghrelin (hunger hormone), lowers leptin (fullness hormone), spikes next-day cravings by hundreds of calories, and worsens insulin resistance. In studies, dieters who slept less lost the same weight but more of it from muscle. Fix your sleep before you fix anything else. The night routine in this plan exists purely to serve this.
Hydration & walkingWater: 2.5–3 L/day. Thirst is routinely misread as hunger; a glass of water before meals modestly reduces intake. Walking: the most underrated fat-loss tool. 8–10k steps daily can burn 200–350 kcal without triggering the hunger that intense cardio does. A 10-minute post-meal walk measurably lowers blood-sugar spikes — perfect for hostel corridors or the campus loop.
Strength training & stressLifting (even bodyweight: squats, push-ups, lunges, resistance bands) tells your body "keep the muscle, burn the fat" and improves insulin sensitivity for 24–48 h after each session. Aim 2–4×/week. Chronic stress raises cortisol → water retention, belly-fat preference, sugar cravings. Ten minutes of anything that calms you (walk, journaling, breathing, calling home) is nutrition too.
Your cycle is not sabotageIn the week before your period, metabolism rises slightly (~100–200 kcal) and so do cravings and water retention — you may "gain" 1–2 kg that vanishes after. This is physiology, not failure. During that week: keep protein high, allow the daily dessert without guilt, prioritise iron (dates, spinach, chana, sprouts) with lemon for absorption, and expect the scale to lie to you. Weigh weekly, same day, same time, after the bathroom, before breakfast — and track the monthly trend, not the number.

Page 04 · The 14-day meal plan
Days 1–14
Built around your real timeline: solid breakfast ~9, a heat-safe mini-lunch box at 1:30 (built for a Chennai afternoon), the main cooked meal at ~6 pm (your multipurpose electric skillet's showtime), a light dinner at 9:30, and a night drink. Tap any dish in Recipes for full instructions. After Day 14, this cycle repeats continuously.

💊 Daily supplement routine (same every day): Vitamin D3 1,000–2,000 IU — 1 tablet right after the 6 pm lunch (D3 absorbs with fat). Vitamin B12 (methylcobalamin 1,500 mcg) — 1 tablet after breakfast on Mon · Wed · Fri · Sun. Brands & details on the Supplements page.

🌅 Wake-up drink — whyRehydrates after 7–8 dry hours (non-negotiable in Chennai's heat and humidity), gently wakes digestion, and replaces the sugary-tea reflex. Jeera, methi and cinnamon waters have modest evidence for digestion and blood-sugar support — but the real win is the habit: water before anything else. None of these "burn fat"; they start the day in control.
🕕 Why lunch at 6 pm works — whyYour biggest meal lands when you're genuinely hungry and finally near your skillet — so it gets planned, not improvised. Front-loading the day with a solid breakfast + 1:30 box keeps blood sugar steady through college, and keeping the 9:30 meal light means you're not sleeping on a heavy stomach — better sleep, better hormones, less next-day hunger.
🌙 Night routine — whyA warm, caffeine-free drink is a sleep cue. Chamomile has mild proven calming effects; warm milk provides tryptophan + casein (slow protein overnight); saunf or peppermint settle a late dinner. Better sleep → lower hunger tomorrow. That's the whole trick.

☀️ Chennai summer rule: nothing dairy or cooked sits out beyond ~2 hours. The 1:30 box is deliberately dry & heat-safe (roasted, whole, PB-based — never curd/paneer). Everything at 6 pm is cooked fresh and eaten hot. Curd is bought fresh the same day, in small packs.

The 6 o'clock kitchen · Lunch every day
Your skillet is the kitchen
The mess gives you exactly one useful thing — chapatis. Everything else, your multipurpose electric skillet cooks better: it sautés vegetables, paneer and tofu in a teaspoon of oil, boils dal, rice, pasta and noodles, and steams in a basket. Here's the system that turns 20–25 minutes at 5:45 into a proper hot meal.

½ Vegetables (in the dish + salad)
¼ Protein (dal/paneer/tofu/soy/curd)
¼ Grain (rice/pasta/noodles/chapati)

Every lunch recipe already follows this ratio — the visual is your check when you freestyle.

The 25-minute skillet workflow

0–3 min: skillet boils water while you chop veg & soak/rinse the grain.
3–15 min: cook the base inside the skillet (dal, rice, pasta, noodles) — lid off near the end so it doesn't foam over.
Or: tip the water out and sauté instead — 1 tsp oil, then onions, veg, paneer/tofu tossed on the hot flat surface for 5–7 min. This is the move for every sautéed-veg bowl you love.
15–20 min: grinder makes the sauce (tomato-onion masala, peanut sauce, green chutney) — stir into the hot base for 2–3 min.
20–25 min: plate, add fresh curd/salad/lemon, eat hot. Wash the skillet immediately — a 90-second rinse now or a fossil by morning.

🫓 The chapati heist guideTake 2–3 chapatis from the mess at their meal time. They're never good as-is — so transform them: tacos (drape over the skillet's dry hot base 40–60 sec per side till stiff, fold), khakhra-chips (crisp fully, snap into chips), or soft wraps (steam 30 sec in the basket to revive). Crisped chapatis keep till next day — fresh-soft ones don't, in this heat.
🔥 One-skillet rulesAdd a splash more water than you think for anything inside the skillet (thin base = quick catching). Stir starchy things (rice/dal) every few minutes. Milk-based sauces: lowest heat, constant stir, or steam-thicken in a bowl in the basket instead. Deglaze stuck bits with hot water right after — never scrub dry.
☀️ No-fridge safetyCook fresh, eat within the hour, no leftovers — in a Chennai hostel room with no fridge, cooked food isn't safe past ~2 hours. Portion the recipes as written (they're single-serve). Curd comes from a fresh evening pack; paneer/tofu are bought morning-of and used the same day.

Page 05 · Recipes
Every recipe, one multipurpose electric skillet
Tap to expand. Your skillet does four jobs: sauté on the flat surface (veg, paneer, tofu in minimal oil), boil-cook inside (dal, rice, pasta, noodles), steam in a basket (chilla-batter, veg, tofu), and dry-crisp (chapatis, bread, toast). Every recipe lists exactly the utensils it needs. Nutrition values are honest estimates (±10%), one serving each. Dairy is bought fresh the same day.

🌅 Breakfasts · solid & warm (9:00)

Classic Poha — Onion, Tomato, Peanuts, Peas & Lemon
Prep 6 minCook 8 minTotal 14 minServes 1Utensils: skillet (inside + basket) · bowl · knife · spoon
IngredientsThick poha — 60 g (¾ cup)Onion — ½ small, finely choppedTomato — 1 small, choppedGreen peas — 3 tbspRoasted peanuts — 1½ tbsp (15 g)Turmeric ¼ tsp · salt · green chilli ½ (optional)Curry leaves 4–5 (optional but optional)Lemon — ½ · corianderGhee or oil — 1 tsp
StepsRinse poha in a bowl under water 10 seconds, drain fully — it should be damp, not soaked.Boil ~2 cm water in the skillet; drop peas + onion into the basket, steam 4 minutes; add tomato for the last 2.Toss the steamed veg with poha, turmeric, salt, chilli, curry leaves and 1 tsp ghee in the bowl.Set the bowl on the basket over steam 2–3 minutes to warm through and fluff.Finish with peanuts, big lemon squeeze, coriander. Fluff with a fork.
≈360 kcal11 g protein54 g carbs12 g fat6 g fibre
Why it works: flattened rice is light but sturdy; peanuts + peas add protein and staying power, and the lemon isn't just taste — vitamin C multiplies iron absorption from the poha. A solid, warm start with no oats in sight.

StepsWhisk besan + water + spices into a smooth, thin pouring batter; fold in all the vegetables.Heat the skillet on medium, brush 1 tsp oil across the flat surface.Pour a ladle and spread thin with the back of the spoon; cook 3 min till the edges lift, flip, 3 min more till golden.Repeat for a second thin chilla. Roll or fold; eat hot with the katori of curd.

Why it works: besan is a low-GI, high-protein flour, and spread thin on the flat skillet it needs only a teaspoon of oil — no deep-fry, no batter-resting drama. Savoury, warm and genuinely filling.

Craving swaps · the section that keeps you on the plan
Junk food, built properly
Here's the truth nobody tells you: diets don't fail at the dining table, they fail at 11 pm when everyone orders pizza. Deprivation has a 100% failure rate over six months — you can white-knuckle it for three weeks, then one bad evening undoes the month. So this section doesn't ask you to resist pizza, burgers, fries, momos or noodles. It hands you the skillet version, with the protein tripled and the oil cut to a teaspoon, ready in 10–20 minutes.

🎯 How to use theseSlot one in 2–4 times a week — as your 6 pm main meal (the bigger ones), or in the dessert/evening slot (the lighter ones). They're calorie-matched to the plan's meals, so a craving swap is the plan, not a cheat on it. Cook them with friends; that's half the point.
🔥 The one ruleMake it properly tasty. Undersalted, joyless "healthy" food is why people quit. Use the real cheese, the peri-peri masala, the chilli flakes, the garlic. Flavour is free — it's the deep-frying and the refined base that cost you, and those are exactly what the skillet replaces.
🧠 Craving first-aidBefore you order: drink a glass of water, wait 10 minutes, and eat something with protein. Most cravings are thirst, boredom, stress or a protein gap wearing a costume. If it's still there after 10 minutes — it's real. Cook the swap, eat it slowly, enjoy it completely.

Training · your 24-week gym plan
Train to keep the muscle, build the engine
The diet decides how much weight you lose; the training decides how much of it is fat. This is a complete beginner-to-confident, 24-week plan for your hostel gym — built for someone who gets breathless after one flight of stairs today and will jog a continuous 15 minutes by month six. Six training days a week, one full rest day, and every session follows the same six-part shape so you never have to wonder what's next.

Read before your first session: start every new exercise light enough to learn the movement, and stop each set with 2 clean reps still in the tank — that's how beginners get strong without getting hurt. If your gym doesn't have a machine listed, use the alternative given. Sharp joint pain is a stop sign (muscle soreness is fine). If you're brand new to lifting, book one session with the gym instructor to check your squat, hinge and press. Breathless-after-stairs is exactly the right starting point — the plan meets you there.

🎯 What you're buildingFat loss (support), muscle you keep & build, cardiovascular stamina, real strength, mobility, posture, and a core that holds you upright. The scale is one metric of ten — strength and stamina are the ones that prove the plan is working even on a stubborn-scale week.
🧱 The six-part sessionEvery day, in order: 1) Warm-up (raise the pulse) → 2) Mobility (open the joints) → 3) Main work (strength or cardio) → 4) Cardio finisher → 5) Cool-down → 6) Stretch. Warm-up and cool-down are never skipped — they're where beginners avoid injury.
📈 How to progressProgressive overload: when you can hit the top of the rep range for all sets with 2 reps to spare, add a little weight next time (or one rep, or one set). Log every session — the plan only works if this week beats last week by a fraction.

The days stay the same; the loads, reps and cardio climb through six phases (table below). Tap any day for its full six-part session.

🛌 Recovery — where the results actually happen

Sleep 7–9 h. The single biggest recovery lever, and it protects muscle in a deficit. The plan's night routine exists for this.
Protein within ~1–2 h of training: the smoothie (add whey), a curd bowl, or a paneer/tofu meal.
Hydrate 2.5–3 L, a little more on heavy-sweat days; a pinch of salt + lemon + water is your free electrolyte drink.
Soreness (DOMS) 24–48 h is normal for the first weeks and fades as you adapt. Sharp or joint pain is not — rest and reassess.
Rest days are training. Take the full Sunday off and don't add "extra" sessions when motivated — consistency for 24 weeks beats heroics for two.

🩸 Training around your cycle
Keep training through your period — movement often eases cramps — but be kind on the heavy days: swap a hard strength or interval day for the Thursday-style mobility + easy-walk session, and come back to full intensity when you feel ready.
Energy and strength often dip pre-period and rebound after — that's physiology, not failure. Prioritise iron-rich foods (spinach, dates, chana, sprouts) with lemon for absorption, as in Palak Dal, and don't judge a whole week by one heavy day. Consistency across the month is what counts.

💡 One-skillet technique corner

Sauté on the flat surface — this is the skillet's superpower a kettle never had. 1 tsp oil, medium heat, then onions → harder veg → paneer/tofu, tossing every minute. Every "sautéed paneer / veg bowl" on this plan is built here. Keep the heat medium so nothing scorches before it softens.
Cook inside the skillet — dal, rice, pulao and noodles go straight in with generous water. Stir every few minutes, keep the lid ajar near the end, and never walk away from milk or starch.
Steam with a basket/trivet + lid: a small steamer basket or trivet turns the skillet into a steamer — chilla batter set into a bowl, vegetables, tofu and paneer steam while something simmers below.
Dry-base crisping: empty, dry skillet on low — chapatis crisp into taco shells, khakhra and chips in 2–3 minutes a side. Watch it the whole time.
Deglaze immediately: after every starchy cook, pour in hot water, swirl, empty, wipe. A starchy film left overnight in Chennai humidity becomes archaeology.
Milk = lowest heat, constant stirring, and pour it out the moment it steams. Or warm the sealed sachet in a bowl of just-boiled water.
Double-blanch sprouts if your stomach is sensitive; squeeze soy chunks hard after soaking — the squeeze is the difference between "paneer's gym friend" and "wet sponge".

🌡 Storing it all through a Chennai summer

No dairy overnight. Buy the day's curd/milk/paneer/tofu that day. Holding paneer a few hours? Submerge it in water in a covered steel dabba in the coolest corner.
Vegetables need air — a ventilated basket or cloth bag, never sealed plastic. Off the floor, out of afternoon sun.
Coriander and mint keep 3–4 days wrapped in a damp cloth; wash only just before using.
Airtight jars for everything dry — humidity turns makhana, murmura, khakhra and poha soft. Two minutes on a dry skillet brings the crunch back.
Jaggery, dates and chocolate soften in the heat. Cosmetic, not spoilage — keep them airtight, away from the sunny wall.
Sprouts always steamed, 4 minutes. Raw sprouts in this humidity are the most common hostel food-poisoning route there is.

💊 Vitamin B12 — Mon · Wed · Fri · Sun, after breakfast
What to buy: Carbamide Forte Methylcobalamin 1,500 mcg (~₹350 for 120 veg tablets — 8 months of doses), or any pharmacy methylcobalamin 1,500 mcg strip. Chewable is fine.

Why you specifically: B12 exists almost only in animal foods; skipping eggs leaves dairy as your sole source, and that's rarely enough. Deficiency creeps in as fatigue, brain fog and tingling hands — and it's extremely common in vegetarian Indian students. This is the one non-negotiable.

💊 Vitamin D3 — daily, right after the 6 pm lunch
What to buy: Uprise-D3 1,000 IU tablets (pharmacy, ~₹110/strip) or HealthKart HK Vitals D3 2,000 IU (~₹400/90). Either works — one tablet, that's it.

Why you specifically: hostel + classes = indoors during peak sun, and most Indian students test low. D3 supports hormones, mood, immunity and insulin sensitivity — all directly relevant to the PCOS picture.

Good idea when convenient: a one-time blood panel (vitamin D, B12, ferritin/iron, thyroid, LFT) — it confirms these doses are right for you and screens the liver question. If a doctor then prescribes a weekly D3 sachet (Calcirol 60,000 IU) for a deficiency, follow that instead of the daily tablet.

Page 12 · Frequently asked questions
The honest FAQ
It’s 6 pm and I have zero energy to cook. Now what?Five-minute fallbacks, in order of effort: sattu shake + banana + peanuts (2 min, no cooking) · PB toast ×2 + milk (3 min) · instant-style thukpa with whatever vegetables are pre-chopped (10 min, one skillet). Any light dinner from the plan also works as an emergency lunch. A tired evening is an inconvenience, not a derailment.
Can I eat out with friends?Yes — plan for roughly one relaxed meal a week. Order what you actually want, eat slowly, skip the sugary drink (that's often 300 kcal alone), and return to the plan at the very next meal. Six months of consistency with weekly flexibility beats six weeks of perfection followed by quitting.
The scale hasn't moved in 10 days. Is it broken? Am I?Neither. Water retention from your cycle, salt, stress or a new workout can mask fat loss for 2–3 weeks. Check: are clothes fitting differently? Are weekly measurements trending down? If truly stalled for 3–4 weeks, add 1,000 daily steps first; only then trim ~100 kcal (usually from grains, never from protein).
I binged last night. Now what?Nothing dramatic. Do not skip today's meals to "compensate" — that restriction is exactly what triggers the next binge. Eat normal Day-X meals, drink water, take a walk, and notice what preceded it (skipped meals? stress? being over-restrictive?). One evening is statistically irrelevant across six months. If bingeing feels frequent or out of control, please talk to a counsellor — college counselling services handle this often and well.
Do I have to exercise for this to work?The deficit works without it, but training decides whether the 20 kg lost is mostly fat (with training) or fat + a worrying amount of muscle (without). That's the whole point of the 24-week plan — it's built for your hostel gym and for a true beginner, starting from walking and bodyweight and progressing to real strength and a continuous run. If the gym is ever shut, bodyweight squats, lunges, push-ups and a resistance band in your room cover a session fully.
Everyone's ordering pizza and I'm dying. What do I do?Cook the skillet pizza — 13 minutes, 340 kcal, tastes like pizza. That's the honest answer, and it's why the craving swaps section exists: burgers, fries, nachos, momos, garlic bread, thick shakes and mug brownies, all rebuilt on your skillet with triple the protein and a teaspoon of oil.And when it's a real night out with friends — go, eat the actual pizza, enjoy it completely. Eat a protein snack before you leave so you don't arrive starving, share the portion, skip the sugary drink, walk home. Then carry on with the very next meal as planned. One meal never undid anyone's progress; quitting on Monday because of Saturday did. Six months only works if there's room in it for your actual life.
Exam week — everything is chaos. Minimum viable plan?Three anchors: (1) protein at breakfast (sattu shake, 4 min), (2) the simplest skillet lunch — thukpa or dal-rice — or the packed box, (3) any dinner from the plan, or a quick besan chilla. Skip the rest guilt-free. Sleep beats a perfect meal during exams — always.
Is all this soy safe for hormones?Yes. Large human studies show normal soy intake (1–2 servings/day) does not disrupt female hormones — if anything, soy isoflavones look mildly favourable in PCOS research. The "soy is dangerous" claims came from rodent megadose studies.
My period changed after a few weeks — what do I do?Slightly irregular cycles can happen during weight change, but a missing or drastically changed period is your body asking for attention: eat at the top of the plan's range (~1,650), ease workout intensity for a couple of weeks, and see a doctor if it persists past two cycles. Health first, always.
What happens after the 20 kg / after 6 months?Reverse slowly: add ~100–150 kcal per week (a roti here, a bigger snack there) over 4–6 weeks until your weight holds steady. Keep the structure — protein breakfast, the 6pm kitchen habit, walks. The plan's endgame is that eating this way stops feeling like a plan.
